title: What Grok and Claude Have to Say about the AI Apocalypse - Nautilus
gist: A Nautilus writer questions AI chatbots (Grok and Claude) about warnings of an AI apocalypse, and asks whether chatbot makers could steer models to calm or to alarm the public for economic gain.

insights.claim: Asking AI chatbots about the risk of an AI apocalypse is epistemically fraught: if the systems could be dangerous, their reassurances are not trustworthy.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Model outputs on AI safety should be read as shaped by the vendor, not as neutral evidence.

insights.claim: The models AI engineers worry about most are not the ones currently available to consumers, so consumer chatbots are a weak proxy for frontier-model risk.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Risk narratives focus on unreleased frontier systems; regulatory and investment attention should track those capabilities rather than consumer products.

insights.claim: Chatbot companies could coach models to tell consumers a gentler story about AI risk, or amplify alarm if that served their economic interests.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Treat AI-risk messaging from vendors as possibly commercially motivated, in either direction.
